jurisdiction.title: County
jurisdiction.description: Which county to ask. There is no auto-detection: resolving a county from an address is a separate problem, and guessing it wrong returns a confident answer about the wrong property. Each county is reached a completely different way, which affects how fast the answer comes and how fresh it is.
enumTitles: San Diego County, CA (live, about 1.5 s, no freshness signal at all)
Duval County, FL (live, about 2 s by parcel id, values are one assessment year behind)
Cook County, IL (live, about 3 s, data one day old, three assessment stages per year)
Travis County, TX (no live endpoint exists; answered from an index of the certified roll, freshest values of the four)

lookupBy.title: Look up by
lookupBy.description: Whether the query is a parcel identifier or a street address. State it explicitly. It is never inferred from the shape of the string, because parcel identifiers have no common format and some of them look like house numbers.

query.title: Parcel identifier or address
query.description:
The parcel identifier or the street address.

There is no national parcel identifier and no per-state one either, so this field cannot be validated beyond 'not empty'. Real examples, one per county: San Diego 3532803300 (ten digits), Duval 0991354355R (ten digits and a letter), Cook 29352110190000 (fourteen digits), Travis 100008 (padded to twelve in the export, type it without the padding). Two counties in the same state do not necessarily agree: another Florida county writes 07702-000-000.

For an address, give as much as you have, for example '7519 Caravaca Ct, Jacksonville, FL 32244'. An address that names a building rather than a single parcel, such as a condominium tower, returns every unit and says so in the flags.

allowContestedOwnerNames.title: Include owner names whose publication is disputed
allowContestedOwnerNames.description:
Whether to return owner names for a county where two publishers of the same parcel data disagree in public about whether the name may be online.

One county here is in that position. In San Diego the county assessor's own service returns the owner name to anyone who asks, unauthenticated, while the joint city and county GIS agency states that California AB1785 bars it from publishing owner name and address information in any publicly accessible online location. This Actor does not settle which one governs.

Left false, which is the default, the parcel comes back complete with the owner name and mailing address withheld and the flag owner_withheld_by_policy explaining why. Set it to true if you have a reason to receive that name; the record then carries owner_name_contested instead, so the dispute travels with the data rather than being lost at the first hop. Counties whose owner names are published without dispute are unaffected either way.

maxResults.title: Maximum records
maxResults.description: How many parcels to return at most. Address lookups are ambiguous by nature: a house number and a street name are not unique across a county of a million parcels, and one condominium address can be hundreds of parcels. When more matched than were returned, the record says so in result_set and flags results_truncated.
